key_insight: Large language models can nearly match expert reliability and outperform laypeople when judging empathic communication, especially when given clear, specific evaluation criteria.
problem_solved: The paper addresses whether automated LLM-based assessments can reliably and scalably evaluate empathic communication, reducing dependence on costly and variable human raters.
method: Evaluate multiple LLMs on empathy assessment tasks across several established frameworks and datasets.
Compare LLM ratings to expert and layperson raters using inter-rater reliability and agreement metrics.
Analyze how the specificity and clarity of evaluation criteria affect performance of both LLMs and human raters.
impact: This enables scalable, consistent evaluation of empathic communication for research and product development, allowing practitioners to use LLMs as reliable evaluators when guidelines are well-defined. It also highlights the importance of precise rubric design for both human and model assessments.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing inter-rater reliability: Experts vs LLMs vs Laypeople
Pipeline diagram: prompt/guideline → LLM assessment → metric comparison
Heatmap or line chart showing LLM performance sensitivity to guideline specificity
Icons representing stakeholders (expert, model, lay rater) and a checklist for rubric clarity
paper_title: When large language models are reliable for judging empathic communication
paper_authors: Aakriti Kumar, Nalin Poungpeth, Diyi Yang, Erina Farrell, Bruce L. Lambert
